claims.title: Ibn Hawqal records Ghana's wealth
claims.summary: The Arab geographer Ibn Hawqal, visiting the western Sudan, describes Ghana's ruler as among the richest kings in the world on account of his gold.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mali: From the gold of Wagadou to the Sahelian republic", terralore.co/country/MLI/chronicle#ev-950-ibn-hawqal-records-ghana-s-wealth, claim TL:MLI:event:950:ibn-hawqal-records-ghana-s-wealth, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Apogee of the gold-and-salt trade
claims.summary: Ghana controls a broad swathe of the western Sahel, acting as the broker between southern goldfields and North African salt caravans.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mali: From the gold of Wagadou to the Sahelian republic", terralore.co/country/MLI/chronicle#ev-1000-apogee-of-the-gold-and-salt-trade, claim TL:MLI:event:1000:apogee-of-the-gold-and-salt-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Almoravids take Kumbi Saleh
claims.summary: Berber Almoravids from present-day Mauritania capture Ghana's chief city, weakening the empire and the trade routes it controlled.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mali: From the gold of Wagadou to the Sahelian republic", terralore.co/country/MLI/chronicle#ev-1076-almoravids-take-kumbi-saleh, claim TL:MLI:event:1076:almoravids-take-kumbi-saleh, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Kirina and the founding of Mali
claims.summary: Sundiata Keita defeats Sumanguru Kanté of the Soso, unifying the Malinke and establishing the Mali Empire with its capital at Niani.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mali: From the gold of Wagadou to the Sahelian republic", terralore.co/country/MLI/chronicle#ev-1235-battle-of-kirina-and-the-founding-of-mali, claim TL:MLI:event:1235:battle-of-kirina-and-the-founding-of-mali, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage to Mecca
claims.summary: Mansa Musa journeys to Mecca with a vast retinue and quantities of gold so great his almsgiving is said to have disrupted Egypt's gold prices, spreading Mali's fame abroad.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mali: From the gold of Wagadou to the Sahelian republic", terralore.co/country/MLI/chronicle#ev-1324-mansa-musa-s-pilgrimage-to-mecca, claim TL:MLI:event:1324:mansa-musa-s-pilgrimage-to-mecca, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Timbuktu and Djenné flourish
claims.summary: Under Mali's mansas the Niger cities grow into major centres of trans-Saharan trade and Islamic scholarship, attracting merchants and scholars.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mali: From the gold of Wagadou to the Sahelian republic", terralore.co/country/MLI/chronicle#ev-1325-timbuktu-and-djenne-flourish, claim TL:MLI:event:1325:timbuktu-and-djenne-flourish, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sonni Ali takes Timbuktu
claims.summary: Sonni Ali captures Timbuktu, and in 1473 Djenné, bringing the Niger trade cities under Songhai control and laying the foundation of the empire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mali: From the gold of Wagadou to the Sahelian republic", terralore.co/country/MLI/chronicle#ev-1468-sonni-ali-takes-timbuktu, claim TL:MLI:event:1468:sonni-ali-takes-timbuktu, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Askia Muhammad founds the Askiya dynasty
claims.summary: A former general seizes power as Askia Muhammad, reorganising the empire and ushering in the golden age of Timbuktu's scholarship.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mali: From the gold of Wagadou to the Sahelian republic", terralore.co/country/MLI/chronicle#ev-1493-askia-muhammad-founds-the-askiya-dynasty, claim TL:MLI:event:1493:askia-muhammad-founds-the-askiya-dynasty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Tondibi ends the Songhai Empire
claims.summary: Moroccan forces under Judar Pasha, armed with firearms, rout the Songhai army at Tondibi near Gao, collapsing the last of the great Niger empires.

sources.label: Moroccan invasion of the Songhai Empire

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mali: From the gold of Wagadou to the Sahelian republic", terralore.co/country/MLI/chronicle#ev-1591-battle-of-tondibi-ends-the-songhai-empire, claim TL:MLI:event:1591:battle-of-tondibi-ends-the-songhai-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bitòn Coulibaly consolidates the Bambara kingdom of Segou
claims.summary: Mamari (Bitòn) Coulibaly transforms a youth society into an army, founding the centralised Bambara state of Segou on the middle Niger.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mali: From the gold of Wagadou to the Sahelian republic", terralore.co/country/MLI/chronicle#ev-1712-biton-coulibaly-consolidates-the-bambara, claim TL:MLI:event:1712:biton-coulibaly-consolidates-the-bambara, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Umar Tal's Tukulor empire conquers Segou
claims.summary: Al-Hajj Umar Tal, leading the Tijaniyya jihad begun in the 1850s, overthrows the Bambara kingdom of Segou and extends the Tukulor empire across the upper Niger.

sources.label: ʿUmar Tal — West African Tukulor Leader & Jihadist

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mali: From the gold of Wagadou to the Sahelian republic", terralore.co/country/MLI/chronicle#ev-1861-umar-tal-s-tukulor-empire-conquers-segou, claim TL:MLI:event:1861:umar-tal-s-tukulor-empire-conquers-segou, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of Umar Tal
claims.summary: The Tukulor leader dies in 1864 near Hamdallahi amid revolt; his successors face mounting French pressure.

sources.label: ʿUmar Tal — West African Tukulor Leader & Jihadist

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mali: From the gold of Wagadou to the Sahelian republic", terralore.co/country/MLI/chronicle#ev-1864-death-of-umar-tal, claim TL:MLI:event:1864:death-of-umar-tal, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Capture of Samori Touré
claims.summary: French forces seize Samori Touré, founder of the Wassoulou Empire and Mali's last great armed resister, ending nearly two decades of war.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mali: From the gold of Wagadou to the Sahelian republic", terralore.co/country/MLI/chronicle#ev-1898-capture-of-samori-toure, claim TL:MLI:event:1898:capture-of-samori-toure, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Colony of French Soudan
claims.summary: The conquered upper Niger is administered as French Soudan within French West Africa, its economy reoriented toward the colonial metropole.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mali: From the gold of Wagadou to the Sahelian republic", terralore.co/country/MLI/chronicle#ev-1920-colony-of-french-soudan, claim TL:MLI:event:1920:colony-of-french-soudan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Mali Federation with Senegal
claims.summary: French Soudan and Senegal join in the short-lived Mali Federation, with Modibo Keïta as a leading figure; it dissolves in August 1960.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mali: From the gold of Wagadou to the Sahelian republic", terralore.co/country/MLI/chronicle#ev-1959-the-mali-federation-with-senegal, claim TL:MLI:event:1959:the-mali-federation-with-senegal, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence of the Republic of Mali
claims.summary: The former French Soudan becomes the independent Republic of Mali; Modibo Keïta becomes its first president the following day.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mali: From the gold of Wagadou to the Sahelian republic", terralore.co/country/MLI/chronicle#ev-1960-independence-of-the-republic-of-mali, claim TL:MLI:event:1960:independence-of-the-republic-of-mali, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Military coup ousts Modibo Keïta
claims.summary: Lieutenant Moussa Traoré leads a coup against the socialist one-party government, beginning 23 years of his rule.

sources.label: Timeline: How Mali went from democracy beacon to instability

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mali: From the gold of Wagadou to the Sahelian republic", terralore.co/country/MLI/chronicle#ev-1968-military-coup-ousts-modibo-keita, claim TL:MLI:event:1968:military-coup-ousts-modibo-keita, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of Moussa Traoré and democratic transition
claims.summary: After a deadly crackdown on protesters on 22 March, officers led by Amadou Toumani Touré oust Traoré; a transition leads to multiparty rule under Alpha Oumar Konaré in 1992.

sources.label: Timeline: How Mali went from democracy beacon to instability

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mali: From the gold of Wagadou to the Sahelian republic", terralore.co/country/MLI/chronicle#ev-1991-fall-of-moussa-traore-and-democratic-transition, claim TL:MLI:event:1991:fall-of-moussa-traore-and-democratic-transition, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Tuareg rebellion, coup and jihadist seizure of the north
claims.summary: The MNLA's January rebellion and a 22 March coup precipitate collapse; AQIM, Ansar Dine and allied jihadists take Timbuktu, Gao and Kidal.

sources.label: Timeline: How Mali went from democracy beacon to instability

claims.title: France launches Operation Serval
claims.summary: As jihadist forces drive toward Bamako, France intervenes militarily, stopping the advance and recapturing the northern cities.

sources.publisher: Combating Terrorism Center at West Point

claims.title: Coup ousts President Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta
claims.summary: Amid mass protests and a worsening insurgency, military officers arrest President Keïta, who resigns; a transitional government is formed.

sources.label: Mali, a Coup within a Coup
Timeline: How Mali went from democracy beacon to instability

claims.title: Second coup brings Assimi Goïta to power
claims.summary: Colonel Assimi Goïta removes the transitional civilian president and prime minister and takes the presidency himself.

sources.label: Mali, a Coup within a Coup
Timeline: How Mali went from democracy beacon to instability
